title: Exposure to non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs during pregnancy and the risk of selected birth defects: a prospective cohort study.
ehr_evidence: Data on NSAID exposure were available from a self-administered questionnaire completed around gestational week 17. Information on pregnancy outcome was obtained from the Medical Birth Registry of Norway.
summary: Prospective cohort study evaluating associations between maternal NSAID use during the first 12 weeks of gestation and selected birth defects using data from the Norwegian Mother and Child Cohort Study linked to the Medical Birth Registry of Norway.
key_findings: No significant association between overall NSAID exposure and selected birth defects (adjusted OR 0.7, 95% CI 0.4–1.1).
No significant associations found for specific NSAID types or congenital heart defects, septal defects, ventricular septal defects, or atrial septal defects.
Increased risk observed for septal defects with multiple NSAID exposure (crude OR 3.9, 95% CI 0.9–15.7), but based on only 2 exposed cases.
population: pregnant women in Norway enrolled in the MoBa cohort (1999-2006), n=67,891 after exclusions
exposure_domain: maternal NSAID use during gestational weeks 0-12
limitations: small number of exposed cases for specific birth defects
